title: Training Bulletin — The Good-Faith Allowance on Re-aged Payment Arrangements Installments
content:
A re-aged installment under Payment Arrangements carries a good-faith allowance measured on the consumer's own payments toward it.

## The rule

The good-faith allowance follows the consumer's own payments on the re-aged installment beyond its scheduled debits, that is its debit card, credit card, check by mail, money order and retail cash payment network payments:

- when they reach at least one third of the installment amount and none of them was returned, the allowance is 31 days;
- when they are above zero but below one third and none was returned, it is 14 days;
- otherwise it is 0 days.

"One third of the installment amount" is the regular installment amount multiplied by 0.3333. The payments are the installment payment entries booked to the re-aged installment on those five channels, added together; "none was returned" means no returned installment payment entry for that installment on those channels. When no missed entry stands on the plan, the good-faith allowance is 0 days.

## Questions and answers (hypothetical figures; regular installment 300.00, so one third is 99.99)

**Q. The consumer paid 100.00 by debit card toward the re-aged installment and nothing came back.**
100.00 reaches 99.99 and none was returned: 31 days.

**Q. The consumer mailed a check for 50.00 toward it.**
Above zero but below 99.99, none returned: 14 days.

**Q. The consumer paid 120.00 by credit card, later charged back.**
One of the own payments was returned: 0 days.

**Q. The only payment on the installment was its scheduled ACH debit.**
An ACH debit is not one of the consumer's own payments listed here; the own payments are zero: 0 days.

## Summary

| Own payments on the re-aged installment | Any of them returned | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| At least the installment amount multiplied by 0.3333 | No | 31 days |
| Above zero, below that amount | No | 14 days |
| Zero, or any of them returned | — | 0 days |
